logline: Three mismatched New York true-crime obsessives bond over a suspicious death in their luxury apartment building and start a podcast - only to keep stumbling into fresh murders.

renewal.note: Renewed for Season 6, set to film in London, announced October 2025 after Season 5 concluded on October 28, 2025.

bollymeter.basis: A perfect 100% Rotten Tomatoes from 107 critics confirmed what audiences felt: the show reinvented the cozy murder-mystery via true-crime meta-satire and a central trio with genuine, effortless chemistry.

pull_quotes.text: Steve Martin has co-created a splendidly funny, involving and youthful series in his mid-70s.
It's very funny about crime podcasting itself, with its meandering storytelling and self-obsession.

seasons.review_body: Season 1 premiered August 31, 2021 on Hulu and earned a rare 100% Tomatometer from 107 critics, with a near-unanimous reception grounded in the show's clever double conceit: it is both a genuinely functional whodunit and a sharp satire of the true-crime podcast genre it inhabits. The three leads, Steve Martin, Martin Short, and Selena Gomez, form a trio whose age-gap chemistry delivers consistent, unforced comedy. The show is described as splendidly funny and involving, with self-aware wit that keeps the meandering podcast storytelling working. Audience scores tracked close behind at 89% Popcornmeter, signaling that the craft impressed viewers as well.

episode_reviews.title: True Crime
episode_reviews.review_body: The 'Only Murders in the Building' pilot accomplishes something structurally elegant: it assembles three unrelated strangers - a faded actor (Steve Martin), a once-celebrated theatre director (Martin Short), and a young woman with a complicated past (Selena Gomez) - and finds a meeting point for them that is both absurdly contrived and emotionally credible. Their shared obsession with a true-crime podcast, combined with the suspicious death of a neighbour in their luxury Upper West Side building, creates a premise that is satirising the genre it inhabits while delivering a functional example of it. The pilot's tonal achievement is its most distinctive: the comedy is warm without being soft, the mystery is functional without being mechanical, and the melancholy underneath the surface is real. Martin and Short have the easy rhythmic comedy of a shared career history; Gomez's Mabel is something trickier - a younger woman carrying grief and damage that the show does not trivialise with jokes. The pilot scored 100% RT - the season held it across all 10 episodes.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The pilot assembles three strangers in an Upper West Side apartment building who share nothing except a love of true-crime podcasts - until a neighbour dies and their obsession becomes an investigation. It establishes tone with remarkable economy: comedy, melancholy, and genuine menace coexisting without friction.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The three discover they have all been listening to the same podcast episode simultaneously - the founding coincidence that kicks the whole premise into gear.

episode_reviews.title: Open and Shut
episode_reviews.review_body: The Season 1 finale delivers on the contract the pilot signed: a mystery that has genuinely tracked its clues, a killer reveal that recontextualises earlier material, and a closing note that is emotionally warmer than the genre usually earns. 'Open and Shut' handles the whodunit resolution with the light touch that defines the whole series - the show is interested in the mystery as a vehicle for character, and the finale prioritises what the investigation has meant for the three principals over the procedural satisfaction of exposing the murderer. Charles, Mabel, and Oliver have become a found family over ten episodes, and the finale earns the sentimentality it permits itself. The reveal works because the show seeded its evidence honestly. The 100% RT season score reflects a first season that managed to be funnier, sadder, and better-plotted than the premise suggested possible.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The season finale resolves the Bunny Folger mystery while expanding the show's emotional stakes considerably. The three principals have become a genuine found family by this point, and the finale earns its warmth without abandoning the comic irreverence that made the season work.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The killer's reveal recontextualises several earlier scenes and proves the show's plotting has been more rigorous than its breezy tone suggested.

bollymeter.basis: A 98% Tomatometer from 122 critics, with the consensus praising a knottier mystery and the trio's deepened character work; the Selena Gomez backstory arc drew particular critical attention.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 arrived June 28, 2022, and earned 98% from 122 critics, close to the perfection of its debut. The RT consensus frames it as getting a new lease on life with a knottier sophomore outing that retains the series' core charm and wit. The mystery this time, centred on a painting and a death at a gala, leans on more structural sophistication, and the show delivers. Guest star Amy Schumer and an expanded role for Cara Delevingne add standout momentum, while the ensemble's core trio remains the emotional engine of the season.
seasons.season_over_season: Maintains the first season's tonal balance while deepening character backstories and raising the central mystery's complexity; the 92% audience Popcornmeter confirmed viewer retention.

bollymeter.basis: 97% Tomatometer from 134 critics; the Broadway theatre setting gave the show's comedic register a richer backdrop, and Meryl Streep's guest arc drew sustained critical enthusiasm.

seasons.review_body: Season 3 shifted the action to a Broadway production's rehearsal period, premiering August 8, 2023 and earning 97% from 134 critic reviews. Meryl Streep's arrival as a stage actress became the dominant talking point. The theatrical setting fits naturally with the show's flair for performance and artifice, and it elevated the season's momentum. Audience scores dipped slightly relative to Season 2, tracking at roughly 88% on the Popcornmeter, but the reviews focused on how the show has sustained its quality across three seasons, a rarity for the genre.
seasons.season_over_season: Trades the apartment building for a Broadway theatre and adds Meryl Streep, creating a season that confirms the show’s standing as a reliable prestige comedy.

bollymeter.basis: 93% Tomatometer; critics noted a slight formulaic settling-in but praised the leads' sustained comedic rapport and a strong late-season stretch.

seasons.review_body: Season 4 premiered August 27, 2024, and held 93% on Rotten Tomatoes. The season develops a more formulaic rhythm by this point in the run, with the mystery structure becoming entirely predictable, but the warm, character-driven comedy remains resilient enough to carry it. The season also adds a meta-layer, with a streaming series being made about the trio, creating a split in how that reflection lands.
seasons.season_over_season: Fourth-season formula creep is audible, but 93% critical approval suggests the leads' chemistry remains strong enough to absorb it.

bollymeter.basis: 89% Tomatometer; RT consensus praised the return to fundamentals and the core trio's undiminished charm even as the show approached five seasons.

seasons.review_body: Season 5 concluded October 28, 2025 with 89% on Rotten Tomatoes - the lowest of any season, but still a comfortable critical majority. The RT consensus noted the season goes back to series fundamentals and reaffirms that the charm of the core trio has not waned. Critics broadly positioned Season 5 as a show comfortably occupying its niche rather than expanding it: pleasant, well-crafted prestige comedy that no longer surprises but still delivers.
seasons.season_over_season: Drops to 89% as the formula reaches five seasons; critical consensus holds that the leads keep the show watchable even without fresh invention.
